To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SwiftCloud provides a causally-consistently client-side data store that scales to high numbers of clients and a large cloud database, while maintaining a high performance and availability.
SwiftCloud provides fast reads and writes to client-side applications using a causally-consistently local cache.
SwiftCloud: • provides causal consistency for client-side applications, • is fast, • is available during faults, and • scales to large databases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: How can we design a distributed database system that provides the best of both worlds: the availability and consistency of a cloud-based database, and the performance, responsiveness, and low latency of a local cache?
providing the best user experience to client-side apps, and the best support to developers, while keeping the system scalable and thrifty.
the design of a distributed object store, that provides fast reads and writes to a large number of unreliable and resource poor clients, using bounded and small metadata.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SwiftCloud provides the first distributed object database with a local causally-consistent cache, and it is thrifty in both resources and metadata.
SwiftCloud is a distributed database that is designed to support client side applications, and provides them with the same level of guarantees as a remote data store, at low cost.
SwiftCloud is the first distributed database that provides fast reads and writes, with a local client-side cache, and with a causal consistency guarantee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new way of thinking about consistency for client-side applications.
the system provides a causal consistency guarantee to client-side applications, with high performance, low latency, high availability, and low cost, while using bounded metadata.
we have developed a new approach for providing consistency for client-side apps that scales well and has low latency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

causally consistent data stores can be built to scale to large numbers of clients with small and bounded metadata, and that client-side apps can benefit from the same guarantees as remote cloud data stores.
client-side apps can be made consistent and fault-tolerance without the need to use a remote database, by using a local cache that can be updated and read from, while maintaining causal consistency.
causal consistency, when implemented correctly, can offer a great solution to the needs of client-side apps.
